summary: In Wisconsin's first open governor's race since 2010, Democratic Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley led Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany 49 to 46 among likely voters in a late September Marquette poll, a narrowing lead. Tiffany and his allies have outspent Crowley's side about 2.5 to 1 according to WisPolitics, and the race turns on taxes and the 3 billion dollar surplus, data centers, abortion and Milwaukee crime.

issues.why: Tiffany wants to return the 3 billion dollar surplus through lasting income and property tax cuts and attacks Crowley's county sales tax increase, while Crowley calls for a broader tax overhaul.
Both back restrictions, with Crowley supporting a pause during a statewide environmental review and Tiffany accusing him of shifting on tech tax incentives.
Crowley proposes a constitutional amendment protecting abortion rights, while Tiffany pledges to keep the 20 week limit and Democrats cite his past six week ban cosponsorship.
Neither would end private school vouchers, but Tiffany may raise income caps while Crowley wants more public school funding.
Tiffany wants local police to coordinate with ICE, while Crowley opposes detainer agreements and wants masked ICE agents banned.

storylines.title: Only debate in Milwaukee
storylines.what: Tiffany hammered county tax hikes and Crowley's dodge on abortion limits, while Crowley tied Tiffany to Trump's tax law and his role in a 2020 election lawsuit.

storylines.title: Ad spending tops 82 million dollars
storylines.what: About 50 million dollars backs Tiffany, though spending was nearly even in the most recent week as new spots on taxes, health care and crime launched.

storylines.title: Poll for school choice group shows Crowley up 4
storylines.what: A YouGov poll of adults for City Forward Collective had Crowley at 46 and Tiffany at 42.

storylines.title: Tiffany side outspends Crowley 2.5 to 1
storylines.what: Tiffany and allies, funded by donors including Diane Hendricks and the Uihleins, spent 54.8 million dollars to Crowley's 21.6 million since the primary.

storylines.title: Crowley pushes abortion amendment
storylines.what: With Sen. Tammy Baldwin, Crowley pledged to pursue a state constitutional amendment on abortion rights, and Tiffany said he would uphold current law and accused Crowley of backing abortion up to birth.

storylines.title: Marquette shows race tightening
storylines.what: Crowley led 49 to 46 among likely voters, down from 5 points, as his unfavorable rating jumped to 44 percent.

events.title: The 3 billion dollar surplus
events.prompt: Wisconsin has a projected 3 billion dollar surplus and voters rank affordability far above other issues. What does the campaign do with it?

opts.label: Invest in schools and care
opts.say: Put the surplus into public schools, child care and a fairer tax code for working families.

opts.label: Split the difference
opts.say: Return some as targeted middle class relief and save the rest for roads and schools.

opts.label: Permanent tax cuts
opts.say: Return it all through a 10 percent income tax cut and property tax relief, not one time checks.

events.title: Data center boom
events.prompt: Large data centers are coming to Wisconsin with tax breaks, and residents worry about power and water. What is the stance?

opts.label: Pause and review
opts.say: Pause new projects during a statewide environmental review and repeal tech tax incentives.

opts.label: Local say
opts.say: Let communities approve projects and require them to pay their own utility costs.

opts.label: Hit the flip flop
opts.say: Back limits but attack the opponent for shifting positions on incentives.

events.title: Abortion limits
events.prompt: The candidates were asked whether they would sign a bill with no gestational limits or a six week ban. What is the answer?

opts.label: Constitutional right
opts.say: Push a constitutional amendment protecting reproductive freedom and say the decision belongs to patients and doctors.

opts.label: Keep current law
opts.say: Promise to uphold the existing 20 week law and not sign stricter bans.

opts.label: Go on offense
opts.say: Accuse the opponent of supporting abortion up to birth based on a 2019 vote.

events.title: Milwaukee crime record
events.prompt: Republican ads attack homicides and taxes in Milwaukee County under the Democrat's watch. How does the campaign respond?

opts.label: Defend the record
opts.say: Point to bipartisan deals that funded police and services and call the attacks distortions.

opts.label: Public safety plan
opts.say: Offer a statewide plan for police hiring and violence prevention.

opts.label: You pay the price
opts.say: Make Milwaukee crime and the sales tax hike the closing argument.

endorsements.who: Sen. Tammy Baldwin campaigned with Crowley

ads.theme: Promises a 10 percent income tax cut, returning the surplus and ending a property tax increase.
An Eau Claire hops farmer says Tiffany follows Trump and voted to cut health care for tax breaks.
Attacks Crowley over a sales tax increase, housing costs and Milwaukee County homicides.
Calls Crowley a complete failure and frames the race as common sense versus incompetence.
